<span id="top"></span>

<p class="category-kicker">Frozen self-supervised backbones with lightweight task adaptation</p>

Large self-supervised vision backbones provide general-purpose features without task-specific labels. A student project should not retrain such a backbone. It should measure what a frozen model already supplies, what a small adapter adds and whether that gain justifies its trainable parameters.

::: {.category-callout}
**Why this category contains one project**

One well-controlled project with two separate tracks is more feasible than several proposals that differ only by backbone or dataset. EuroSAT RGB is the accessible Bachelor route; MVTec dense anomaly localisation or multispectral EuroSAT is the higher-risk Master route.
:::

## Learn first and find ideas

- Core reading: [DINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14294), [DINOv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193), the [DINOv2 model card and code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov2), [DINOv3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10104) and [AnomalyDINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14529).
- Data and model hubs: [MVTec AD](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad), [EuroSAT](https://github.com/phelber/EuroSAT), [Hugging Face models](https://huggingface.co/models) and [timm](https://github.com/huggingface/pytorch-image-models).
- Keep zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot and full-shot anomaly results separate, and never compare an image-level metric directly with a pixel-level metric.

## 4.1  Adapting DINO backbones for land cover or industrial anomalies {#project-4-1}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Image classification or image/pixel anomaly detection</span>
<span class="meta-label">Recommended level</span><span class="meta-value">BSc or MSc with separate tracks</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Moderate; frozen ViT-S practical on 8 GB, dense MSc work may need more</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Oquab et al., [DINOv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193), 2023</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Use a pretrained self-supervised vision transformer as a frozen feature extractor. A small head or adapter is trained for a specialised task. The research question is not whether the huge backbone can be retrained, but how far frozen features go and whether an adapter contributes beyond a newer backbone.
:::

**Project goal.** Quantify the trade-off among task performance, number of trainable parameters and supervision. Choose **one** track: EuroSAT RGB land-cover classification or MVTec industrial anomaly detection/localisation.

**Data.** **BSc/default classification track:** [EuroSAT](https://github.com/phelber/EuroSAT), 27,000 Sentinel-2 patches in 10 classes. Use the **RGB** version for ordinary DINO backbones; the 13-band version requires an explicit multispectral adapter and is a separate MSc question. **MSc anomaly track:** [MVTec AD](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad), more than 5,000 images in 15 categories with pixel masks, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial research.

**Methods and starting code.** Default to DINOv2 ViT-S/14 from the [official Apache-2.0 repository and model card](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov2). Compare frozen linear/MLP probes, k-NN or [AnomalyDINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14529) patch similarity, and a lightweight multi-scale adapter. DINOv3 is optional through the [official repository](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov3); its weights are gated under a custom Meta licence.

**Required baselines.** From-scratch CNN, ImageNet-pretrained ResNet or ViT, frozen DINOv2 with no adapter, lightweight adapter and full fine-tuning only if hardware permits. On MVTec, include a simple nearest-neighbour patch baseline and keep zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot and full-shot protocols separate.

**Evaluation.** EuroSAT: top-1 accuracy, macro-F1, label-efficiency curve and trainable parameters. MVTec: image AUROC plus pixel AUROC/PRO or pixel F1-max, reported by category and protocol. Measure inference memory/latency. Never compare a one-shot image metric directly with a zero-shot pixel metric.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor scope.** Use EuroSAT RGB. Compare a frozen DINOv2 ViT-S linear probe with an ImageNet-pretrained CNN and, if feasible, a small adapter at several label budgets.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question and contribution.** Choose one question. **Dense anomaly route:** can a supervised multi-scale adapter over frozen patch tokens improve few-shot localisation at a fixed label and parameter budget, and does the gain remain after switching DINOv2 to DINOv3? **Remote-sensing route:** can a small multispectral input adapter exploit 13 bands without full backbone fine-tuning? Report cross-version or cross-band ablations so the adapter's value is isolated.
:::

**Feasibility and guardrails.** Do not attempt DINOv3 ViT-7B. DINOv2 is ungated and Apache 2.0; build the pipeline on it first. DINOv3's licence is non-standard and gated but not stated as categorically non-commercial; an industry use requires institutional/legal review. MVTec itself is non-commercial, so it cannot serve as an industry dataset without separate permission.
